source_user: A service receives a mix of short prompts and long generations. Design an evaluation plan that reports TTFT, TPOT, throughput, queueing, and P99 latency. Scenario variant 212: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: separate prefill and decode behavior; fix workload distribution; report warmup; use repeated trials; capture GPU memory and request-level traces.
corrected_answer:
Treat scenario variant 212 as an evaluation-design request, not evidence of a platform result. Assume two otherwise identical deployments with the same model/tokenizer, precision, hardware, software build, scheduler settings, and observability; use an immutable replayable trace. Stratify results by prompt length, requested output length, arrival/concurrency load, and cache state. Randomize matched A/B blocks, keep routing, batching, admission policy, and autoscaling fixed, declare and discard warm-up, and run at least five paired repetitions with fixed seeds and a pre-registered analysis.

Falsifiable hypothesis for variant 212: the candidate increases SLO-goodput (correct requests per second meeting declared latency and error targets) by at least 10% without increasing error rate or end-to-end P99 by more than 5%. Estimate paired differences with confidence intervals; call the hypothesis unsupported if the predefined bounds are not met. Capture synchronized ingress, admission, queue release, prefill start/end, first token, each decode-token timestamp, completion, timeout, cancellation, retry, and correctness outcome. Report queue-inclusive TTFT (first token minus ingress) separately from compute-only TTFT (first token minus prefill start); define TPOT as decode elapsed time divided by generated-token count with explicit first/last-token conventions; also report output tokens/s, queue wait, end-to-end latency, and P99 over a declared completed/request denominator. Separate prefill and decode distributions and state missing, timed-out, cancelled, and retried-request handling.

Measure request rate, concurrency, batch sizes, prompt/output token counts, KV-cache hit/eviction state, GPU memory, utilization, power, clocks, temperature, host CPU/memory, network, and queue depth. Check output correctness and record OOMs, scheduler errors, deadline misses, and retries; do not silently drop failures. Control for thermal throttling, cache warmth, tokenization, background load, placement, clock drift, and trace imbalance. Require raw request traces, build/config/workload manifests, synchronized telemetry, correctness labels, and uncertainty analysis before claiming improvement. Canary the candidate with error and latency guardrails; halt and revert to the known good deployment on elevated errors, OOMs, deadline violations, or instability. This is provisional calibration, not expert gold or authoritative capability evidence.
risks: P99 and goodput depend on workload strata, denominators, warm-up, cache state, and shared-resource confounders.
The 10% and 5% thresholds are prespecified criteria, not measured facts.
Provisional calibration is not expert gold or authoritative domain capability.
evidence_required: Immutable trace and exact build/config/workload manifests
Synchronized raw request lifecycle and GPU/CPU/power/thermal telemetry
At least five randomized paired repetitions with correctness, failure, and uncertainty analysis
